topics.title: Five components of a relational DBMS and the life of a query
topics.summary: Five components: Client Communications Manager, Process Manager, Relational Query Processor, Transactional Storage Manager and shared components; the life of a query crosses all of them (ARCH p.4-7).

topics.title: Process models: process per worker, thread per worker, pool; PostgreSQL uses process per worker
topics.summary: Process per worker, thread per worker and pool; PostgreSQL uses one process per connection (ARCH p.12-22; PG16 p.2291-2292).

topics.title: Admission control and thrashing
topics.summary: Above a certain load throughput drops (thrashing); admission control limits connections and uses the optimizer's memory/CPU/I-O estimates (ARCH p.22-24).

topics.title: Shared-memory, shared-nothing, shared-disk and NUMA
topics.summary: Shared-memory, shared-nothing (horizontal partitioning hash/range/round-robin/hybrid; partial failure: bring everything down, Data Skip or redundancy such as chained declustering, n-1 nodes do n/(n-1) of the work, ARCH p.29), shared-disk (does not require partitioning; corrupted data reaches all nodes; needs a distributed lock manager and cache coherence, ARCH p.30-31), NUMA (optimize above 1.5:1 to 2:1, ARCH p.32).

topics.title: Parser, authorization and rewrite (views, predicates, subqueries)
topics.summary: Rewriter with no data access: view expansion, constant arithmetic, logical/transitive predicates, redundant join elimination, subquery flattening and partition elimination by unsatisfiable predicate (ARCH p.39-42).

topics.title: Cost-based optimizer (Selinger/System R) and extensions
topics.summary: Selinger-style block optimization (dynamic programming, left-deep), statistics/histograms, top-down search, two-phase parallelism and auto-tuning (ARCH p.42-48; REDBK p.16). Volcano/Cascades, Orca and Calcite in Red Book ch. 7 (REDBK p.33); in ARCH 'Volcano' only appears in the reference list (p.114).

topics.title: Iterator model (init/get_next/close), BP-tuples and M-tuples, Halloween problem
topics.summary: Iterator model init/get_next/close; one thread executes the plan, with no queues or rate matching between iterators (contrast with networks) and with PostgreSQL code cited as an example (ARCH p.49); BP-tuples and M-tuples; exchange iterators for parallelism; straight-line DML plans (ARCH p.48-52).

topics.title: Nested loop, merge join and hash join in PostgreSQL
topics.summary: Nested loop, merge join and hash join in PostgreSQL, with EXPLAIN examples (PG16 p.2294, p.545-547).

topics.title: Planner cost parameters and statistics (pg_stats, MCV, histograms)
topics.summary: Cost parameters, pg_statistic/pg_stats, work_mem, how to read EXPLAIN ANALYZE (loops, Rows Removed) and extended statistics (PG16 p.482, p.548-557, p.682-685).

topics.title: Prepared statements, typical values and plan cache
topics.summary: Prepared plans and plan cache; 'typical' values in the estimate; IBM prioritizes predictability, Microsoft recompiles more (ARCH p.47-48).

topics.title: Buffer pool: frames, hash table, dirty bit, pin count, replacement
topics.summary: Frame vector with hash table, dirty bit, pin count; LRU/CLOCK do badly on scans; LRU-2; PG: shared_buffers 128 MB, bgwriter, pg_buffercache (ARCH p.74-76; PG16 p.653-659, p.2885).

topics.title: Spatial and temporal control: raw vs file, OS buffering
topics.summary: Spatial control (sequential 10-100x random), raw device versus large file (6% in TPC-C; 1% with Direct I/O), temporal control and double OS buffering, page size (ARCH p.70-74).

topics.title: ACID and serializability
topics.summary: ACID as an informal mnemonic; serializability = equivalence to serial execution (ARCH p.79-80).

topics.title: Strict 2PL, MVCC and optimistic control (OCC)
topics.summary: Strict 2PL, MVCC and OCC: how each handles conflicts (ARCH p.80-82; REDBK p.17-18).

topics.title: Lock manager, latches and deadlock detection
topics.summary: Lock table, mode matrix, deadlock detection by cycles; latches are lighter, with no detection, and a latch deadlock is a bug (ARCH p.82-84).

topics.title: ANSI isolation levels, phantom, cursor stability, snapshot isolation, read consistency
topics.summary: Four ANSI levels, phantom, cursor stability, snapshot isolation (first committer wins), read consistency (ARCH p.84-88; REDBK p.28-29).

topics.title: Latching in B+-trees, next-key locking, interdependencies
topics.summary: 2PL on index pages would lock the root until commit; latch schemes: conservative, latch coupling/crabbing (lock the child and only then release the parent; ARIES-IM; B+-tree only) and right-link (link to the right neighbor, no coupling, 'move right' after a split; PostgreSQL's GiST is based on Kornacker's right-link); splits can be redo-only via nested top actions; right-link assumes pages are not merged; next-key locking and its excess of locks (ARCH p.92-97).

topics.title: Three WAL rules and DIRECT STEAL/NOT-FORCE
topics.summary: Three WAL rules, STEAL/NO-FORCE and physiological logging (ARCH p.88-90); WAL in PostgreSQL (PG16 p.898-902). Internals: LSN in bytes, 16 MB segments in pg_wal, the 8 kB page only changes at compile time, numbering does not wrap around, move pg_wal with the server stopped + symbolic link, disks that lie about writes (PG16 p.903).

topics.title: ARIES: repeating history, three phases (Red Book summary), fuzzy checkpoints
topics.summary: ARIES: analysis, redo and undo, repeating history, fuzzy checkpoint (REDBK p.16-18; ARCH p.90-93).

topics.title: Checkpoints, checkpoint_timeout, max_wal_size in PostgreSQL
topics.summary: Checkpoint every checkpoint_timeout (5 min) or max_wal_size (1 GB); completion_target 0.9; full page writes after the checkpoint (PG16 p.900-901).

topics.title: Asynchronous commit, fsync=off and non-durable settings
topics.summary: Asynchronous commit loses the last transactions without corrupting; fsync=off can corrupt; non-durable settings; UNLOGGED tables (PG16 p.899-900, p.563, p.897). Details: per-transaction mode; DROP TABLE and two-phase commit are always synchronous; immediate shutdown = crash and loses asynchronous commits; commit_delay is ignored in asynchronous commit; checkpoint skipped without new WAL (PG16 p.899-900).

topics.title: Isolation and MVCC in PostgreSQL (RC, RR, Serializable/SSI)
topics.summary: Read Committed is the default; Repeatable Read = snapshot isolation; Serializable = SSI with error 40001 and retry (PG16 p.525-531).

topics.title: Tuple header (xmin, xmax, ctid), snapshot and 32-bit XID
topics.summary: Tuple header (t_xmin, t_xmax, t_cid, t_ctid) and snapshots (PG16 p.2574-2575, p.429). CTID = page + item identifier index, stable within the page (PG16 p.2574).

topics.title: Index types: B-tree, Hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN, BRIN, bloom
topics.summary: B-tree, Hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN and BRIN; B-tree by default; only B-tree is UNIQUE (PG16 p.467-470, p.2508-2566).

topics.title: Multicolumn, partial, expression, INCLUDE/covering, index-only scan
topics.summary: Multicolumn, partial, expression indexes, INCLUDE, index-only scan; evaluate with ANALYZE and EXPLAIN (PG16 p.470-482).

topics.title: GIN, fast update and JSONB (jsonb_ops, jsonb_path_ops)
topics.summary: GIN for jsonb: jsonb_ops (default: ?, @>, jsonpath) and jsonb_path_ops (only @>, @?, @@; smaller and more specific); fastupdate and pending list (PG16 p.223-225, p.2545-2550).

topics.title: BRIN: block ranges, pages_per_range (default 128), summary
topics.summary: BRIN: summary per block range, pages_per_range 128; entries = pages / pages_per_range; only helps with physical correlation; 1 TiB = 134,217,728 pages = 1,048,576 entries with 128 [derived] (PG16 p.2552, p.1758). pageinspect (PG16 p.2878-2879): brin_metapage_info, brin_revmap_data, brin_page_items; the manual's example reads get_raw_page(...,5) but the TIDs point to page 6 (inconsistency recorded).

topics.title: Hash index: 32-bit hash, equality only, recoverable
topics.summary: Hash: equality only, no uniqueness, one column (PG16 p.469, p.2565).

topics.title: VACUUM: reasons, VACUUM FULL, statistics, visibility map
topics.summary: VACUUM reclaims space, updates the visibility map and freezes XIDs; VACUUM FULL requires ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (PG16 p.788-791).

topics.title: XID wraparound, freezing, warnings at 40 million and refusal at 3 million
topics.summary: 32-bit XID: mandatory vacuum before 2 billion; warnings at 40 million and refusal below 3 million (PG16 p.791-796).

topics.title: Autovacuum: launcher, workers, threshold formula and parameters
topics.summary: Threshold 50 + 0.2 x tuples; per-table tuning; even when disabled, it fires for wraparound (PG16 p.702-704, p.796-797).

topics.title: Page layout (8 kB), FSM, visibility map, forks, 1 GB segments
topics.summary: 8 kB page, 24-byte header (Table 73.3: pd_lsn 8, checksum 2, flags 2, lower 2, upper 2, special 2, pagesize_version 2, prune_xid 4), item identifiers never move until freed (stable CTID), a single page size per installation, FSM and visibility map (PG16 p.2567-2576).

topics.title: TOAST: 2 kB threshold, strategies, 18-byte pointer
topics.summary: TOAST: large values out of line, threshold ~2 kB, four strategies (PG16 p.2569-2571).

topics.title: Heap-only tuples (HOT)
topics.summary: HOT: possible when the UPDATE does not change columns referenced by the table's indexes, NOT COUNTING summarizing indexes (the only one in core is BRIN), and there is room in the old row's page; it avoids new index entries (summarizing indexes may still need an update) and allows removing old versions during normal operation, even in SELECT; a lower fillfactor increases the chance, but HOT still occurs without it; monitor in pg_stat_all_tables (n_tup_hot_upd) (PG16 p.2576, p.868-869).

topics.title: Declarative partitioning (range, list, hash)
topics.summary: Declarative partitioning (range/list/hash), PK must include the partition key, ATTACH with CHECK, DETACH CONCURRENTLY, pruning at planning and execution time (including what happens without an upper bound), good practices on the number of partitions (PG16 p.132-145).

topics.title: WITH RECURSIVE, SEARCH, CYCLE and ltree
topics.summary: WITH RECURSIVE, cycles and ltree (PG16 p.173-178).

topics.title: Naive Trees: Adjacency List (parent_id), limits, maintenance, legitimate uses
topics.summary: Adjacency List: parent_id; descendant queries require recursion; suitable if only parent/direct children are needed (ANTI-TREE p.5-11).

topics.title: SQL Injection: antipattern, escaping, parameters and their limits, procedures, frameworks, indirect injection
topics.summary: Injection by interpolation; parameters are a strong but not universal defense; identifiers and lists cannot be parameterized (ANTI-INJ p.5-14; PG16 p.971-972, p.984-985, p.1364-1365).

topics.title: Anatomy of an antipattern and the book's table of contents
keywords: o que nao esta no livro
topics.summary: Anatomy of a chapter of the book (Objective, Antipattern, Recognize, Legitimate Uses, Solution) and scope of the book: it does not cover performance, administration (backup, security) or NoSQL (ANTI-INT p.8-9).

topics.title: Red Book: architecture, in-memory OLTP, columnar stores, System R/Postgres/Gamma
topics.summary: Red Book: column stores dominate data warehouses, OLTP moves toward main memory, 2PL should lose ground, NoSQL tends to merge into SQL (REDBK p.2, p.21-22) [DATED]. Ch. 1 (REDBK p.1-2): XML became a niche; JSON is good for sparse data and a disaster as a general hierarchical format; Google abandoned MapReduce; Impala (SQL over HDFS); data lake = junk drawer; column stores 1-2 orders of magnitude faster than row stores.

topics.title: Data warehouses in ARCH: bitmap, fast load, materialized views, OLAP, star schema
topics.summary: Data warehouses: bitmap indexes, bulk load, materialized views, OLAP/cubes, star/snowflake schema (ARCH p.56-62).

topics.title: Catalog, memory allocator, disks, replication and utilities
topics.summary: ARCH section 7: catalog, memory allocator, disks/RAID, replication, utilities (ARCH p.100-110).

topics.title: Weak isolation is prevalent in practice (Red Book ch.6)
topics.summary: Weak isolation is the default in most databases (3 of 18 serializable by default); Flexcoin; ORMs that assume serializability; SELECT FOR UPDATE and false conflicts are 'highly error-prone'; NoSQL x RDBMS (irony on p.30); Dynamo: non-transactional, no atomics, reconciliation by the application, eventual consistency (REDBK p.28-30).

topics.title: Halloween problem (an UPDATE that rereads its own changes)
keywords: um comando nao ve as proprias atualizacoes
topics.summary: Naive plan: an IndexScan on the updated column feeds the Update; the tuple moves to the right in the B+-tree and is found again (several raises). SQL forbids seeing its own updates. Solutions: avoid an index on the updated column or materialize RIDs in a temporary file before updating (pipelining requires multiversioning). The footnote says it has nothing to do with the phantom problem. PostgreSQL: the manual describes no technique of its own (t_cid at PG16 p.2575 is only a hint).

topics.title: Bitmap indexes in data warehouses (1 bit vs ~40 bits per record)
topics.summary: For a 2-valued attribute, a bitmap uses 1 bit per record against ~40 bits (value + pointer) in a B+-tree; conjunctive filters become bitmap intersections; updates are expensive, so it only suits warehouses. PostgreSQL has no persistent bitmap index (bitmap is a scan type).

topics.title: Columnar storage: factor 16, compression, 16 B header and '50-100x'
topics.summary: REDBK p.21: fact with ~100 attributes and a query touching ~6 => 16x less data read [100/6 = 16.7, derived]; better compression per column; no per-record header (16 B in SQL Server); inner loop paid per column; 'column stores 50-100x faster' is a 2015 opinion [DATED], not a measurement, and does not hold for OLTP. ARCH p.62: good for wide tables and append-mostly; a problem for OLTP (aligning rows across columns).

topics.title: Access methods: SARG, RID and primary storage
topics.summary: Access methods are iterators with a SARG (column operator constant) to filter inside the layer (avoids pin/unpin and per-tuple copies). A physical RID makes moving rows expensive; DB2 uses a forwarding pointer; SQL Server and Oracle use the primary key in secondary indexes when the B+-tree is the primary storage.

topics.title: Extensibility: ADTs, XML/JSON, text search, wrappers
topics.summary: Abstract types driven by the catalog; expression indexes and extensible access (GiST); XML by ADT or shredding; text search by inverted file, usually asynchronous (PostgreSQL offers a transactional option); rule-based optimizers; remote sources as tables.

topics.title: RAID, SAN, write cache and 'a well-tuned OLTP is not I/O-bound'
topics.summary: ARCH p.74: throughput of a well-tuned OLTP is normally not limited by I/O (enough disks and RAM; memory bottlenecks remain). ARCH p.105-106: RAID/SAN complicate the DBMS (performance after a failure, write cache can corrupt), RAID 5 has poor writes and mirroring (RAID 1) is better for databases; Gamma's chained declustering does better than RAID.

topics.title: Catalog (metadata as tables)
topics.summary: The catalog is stored as tables of the database itself; hot parts are kept denormalized in memory; one ERP had more than 60,000 tables.

topics.title: Context-based memory allocator and operator memory
topics.summary: Memory contexts (create, allocate, delete, reset) replace per-phase garbage collection (parser, optimizer, executor); DB2 for zSeries fixes RAM per operator, SQL Server automates it.

topics.title: Replication (physical, trigger-based and log-based) in ARCH
topics.summary: Three schemes: physical (does not scale), trigger-based (performance penalty) and log-based (preferred: low overhead, incremental, transactionally consistent replicas); log-based has two techniques (generate SQL or ship records to a destination in perpetual recovery).

topics.title: Online utilities: statistics, reorganization, fuzzy backup, bulk load, monitoring
topics.summary: Utilities must run online; 'fuzzy' backup with the log; bulk load via storage manager code; virtual monitoring tables and resource governors.

topics.title: json x jsonb (PostgreSQL 16)
topics.summary: json stores the exact text (preserves whitespace, order and duplicate keys; reparsed on each use); jsonb is decomposed binary, slightly slower on input and much faster on processing, indexable; the manual recommends jsonb except for specialized needs. Any update locks the whole row: limit the document size. GIN: jsonb_ops (? @> jsonpath) and jsonb_path_ops (smaller, only @> @? @@).

topics.title: Backup, WAL archiving and PITR (PostgreSQL 16)
topics.summary: Three approaches: SQL dump, file-system backup and continuous archiving. PITR = base backup + archived WAL + a target after the end of the backup; 16 MB segments; archive_timeout (~1 min is reasonable) forces a segment switch but the file stays 16 MB [60 s => 1,440 files/day = 22.5 GiB/day, derived]; WAL does not restore postgresql.conf; recovery requires emptying pg_wal, restore_command and recovery.signal and creates a new timeline. pg_dump is not suitable for PITR. pg_dump -j only in directory format; pg_restore -j works with custom or directory (PG16 p.803); -Fc is not a psql script.

topics.title: High availability and replication (overview, PostgreSQL 16)
topics.summary: Comparison of solutions: shared disk (no copy; the disk array is a single point of failure), block replication, WAL shipping (whole server; asynchronous has a loss window), logical replication (per table; does not replicate DDL or sequences; triggers do not fire on the subscriber), triggers, SQL middleware, multimaster. PostgreSQL does not offer synchronous multimaster. Streaming, synchronous replication, failover, hot standby and pg_rewind: see topics pg-streaming-replication-slots, pg-synchronous-replication, pg-failover-stonith, pg-hot-standby and pg-rewind-wal-log-hints.

topics.title: Row-Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL 16
topics.summary: With no policies, enabling RLS denies everything; the table owner is normally not filtered (FORCE subjects it); superusers and BYPASSRLS ignore it; permissive policies combine by OR and restrictive ones by AND; USING without WITH CHECK applies to both; TRUNCATE and REFERENCES are not subject to RLS; referential integrity ignores RLS (covert channel); row_security=off makes the server raise an error instead of filtering (backups); sub-SELECTs in policies can have race conditions. CREATE POLICY (PG16 p.1776-1779): PERMISSIVE (OR) x RESTRICTIVE (AND), only restrictive = nothing accessible; SELECT without WITH CHECK, INSERT only WITH CHECK, DELETE only USING; UPDATE/DELETE that read columns also require a SELECT policy; ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and MERGE raise an error instead of filtering; Table 292 (filter x check).

topics.title: Triggers (PostgreSQL 16)
topics.summary: A trigger runs in the same transaction as the command; a per-row BEFORE that returns NULL skips the operation on that row (return NEW/OLD so as not to interfere); the return of a per-row AFTER is ignored; per-statement triggers must return NULL; alphabetical order; WHEN; recursion is the programmer's responsibility; an UPDATE that moves a row between partitions becomes DELETE+INSERT. CREATE TRIGGER (PG16 p.1854-1855): default FOR EACH STATEMENT, UPDATE OF col fires based on the SET list (a change made by BEFORE does not count), WHEN without subquery and no WHEN in INSTEAD OF, BEFORE does not see system columns (ctid), per-row trigger clones on partitions.

topics.title: SQL Antipatterns: chapter and solution titles (table of contents only)
topics.summary: The PDF has only the table of contents: chapter and solution titles (e.g.: ch. 10 Rounding Errors -> Use NUMERIC Data Type; ch. 11 31 Flavors -> Specify Values in Data; ch. 6 EAV -> Model the Subtypes; ch. 17 Poor Man's Search Engine -> Use the Right Tool for the Job). The text of the chapters (except 1, 3 partial and 21 partial) is not in the PDFs.

topics.title: Red Book ch. 2: legacies of System R, Postgres and Gamma (Stonebraker's opinions)
topics.summary: System R: biggest legacy = the transaction manager (Jim Gray), then the dynamic-programming optimizer; Postgres: abstract data type (ADT) system, time travel tried and did not work well; Gamma: shared-nothing and hash join (REDBK p.14-15) [DATED].

topics.title: Red Book ch. 3: atomic commit (2PC, Presumed Abort/Commit) x consensus (Paxos, Raft, Paxos Commit)
topics.summary: AC: any participant can vote NO and everyone aborts; consensus: any proposal will do if everyone agrees; AC and consensus can block; consensus underpins replication, AC transactions across partitions; Paxos Commit (Gray and Lamport, 2006) (REDBK p.18-19) [DATED].

topics.title: CREATE SUBSCRIPTION: parameters, defaults and notes (PG16 command)
topics.summary: Defaults: connect, create_slot, enabled, copy_data = true; binary = false; slot_name = subscription name; connect=false forces create_slot/enabled/copy_data to false (create the slot, enable and refresh by hand); slot_name NONE requires enabled and create_slot false; binary is type-specific and the initial sync requires send/receive; does not run in a transaction block with a slot (PG16 p.1811-1814).

topics.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, INVALID index, partitioned tables and command notes
topics.summary: Two scans and waiting for transactions; failure leaves an INVALID index (ignored by queries, but with update cost; on a unique index it still enforces uniqueness); recover with DROP INDEX or REINDEX CONCURRENTLY; only one CIC per table; does not run in a transaction block; partitioned: per partition and then ON ONLY/ATTACH (PG16 p.1758-1760).

topics.title: Text search 12.9: GIN x GiST (siglen, weight recheck) and ts_lexize
topics.summary: GIN preferred (inverted index, lexemes only, recheck for weights); lossy GiST with signature (siglen 124, maximum 2024); maintenance_work_mem speeds up GIN build and not GiST build; ts_lexize takes one token (PG16 p.519-520).

topics.title: VACUUM command: FULL, PARALLEL, TRUNCATE, INDEX_CLEANUP and other options
topics.summary: PARALLEL = eligible indexes limited by N and by max_parallel_maintenance_workers, only with 2 or more indexes; TRUNCATE returns empty pages to the OS and requires ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; INDEX_CLEANUP OFF only for imminent wraparound (the failsafe is preferable); FULL rewrites with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; does not run in a transaction block (PG16 p.2063-2067).

topics.title: Rule system: views, security_barrier, LEAKPROOF and rules x triggers
topics.summary: A view without security_barrier leaks rows through a cheap function in the planner; the barrier costs performance; only LEAKPROOF goes up before the filter; EXPLAIN, timing and statistics still leak; a rule does not implement FK (NOTHING silently discards): use a trigger (PG16 p.1343-1344).

topics.title: cert, clientcert and RADIUS authentication (pg_hba.conf)
topics.summary: cert only on SSL, no password prompt, cn x user with map; clientcert is redundant with cert; RADIUS: radiusports default 1812 (no accounting), radiusidentifiers default postgresql, secret with 16 or more characters (PG16 p.732, p.746-747).

topics.title: pg_collation catalog: collprovider, collversion and unique key
topics.summary: collprovider d/c/i; collversion detects a definition change; unique key (collname, collencoding, collnamespace); the qualified name schema.name is enough to identify the collation (PG16 p.2309).

topics.title: COPY: server-side file x \copy, triggers/CHECK, identity, error and space, partitions/RLS/WHERE (PG16 COPY command, notes)
topics.summary: File and PROGRAM are read/written by the server (the postgres OS user), only for superusers or pg_read_server_files/pg_write_server_files/pg_execute_server_program; psql's \copy uses STDIN/STDOUT and the client's file; a relative path in COPY FROM is relative to the server process; COPY FROM fires triggers and CHECK, does not fire rules; identity columns: COPY FROM always writes the file's value, like OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE (the page does not say it rejects); with no column list, generated columns are skipped (p.1697); stops at the first error and old rows occupy invisible disk space (VACUUM) (PG16 p.1700). Notes (p.1699): COPY TO only from plain tables and does NOT copy children or partitions (COPY t TO = SELECT * FROM ONLY t; use COPY (SELECT * FROM t) TO for a partitioned table, inheritance or view); COPY FROM accepts plain, foreign, partitioned tables and views with INSTEAD OF INSERT; RLS SELECT policies apply to COPY TO, COPY FROM is not supported with RLS; WHERE (FROM only) accepts no subquery or generated column and does not see changes made by the COPY itself (PG16 p.1699).

topics.title: Window functions: evaluated after GROUP BY/HAVING; order and sorting (PG16 7.2.5)
topics.summary: Windows are evaluated after grouping, aggregation and HAVING (they see the group rows); windows with equivalent PARTITION BY/ORDER BY see the same order; different specifications have no guarantee and the sort between passes does not preserve ties; the output comes out ordered by some window but this must not be relied on: use a top-level ORDER BY (PG16 p.168).

topics.title: GREATEST/LEAST ignore NULL; array operators (@> and duplicates); intarray module (PG16 9.18.4, 9.19, F.20)
topics.summary: GREATEST/LEAST ignore NULL and only return NULL if all are NULL (a deviation from the SQL standard); array comparison is element by element; @> does not treat duplicates specially (ARRAY[1] and ARRAY[1,1] contain each other); intarray: integer arrays without NULL (error if there is NULL), uniq removes only adjacent ones (use with sort), trusted module (PG16 p.385, p.2854).

topics.title: DROP OWNED and REASSIGN OWNED (PG16 DROP OWNED command)
topics.summary: DROP OWNED removes the objects of the CURRENT database owned by the role and revokes its privileges (including on shared objects); RESTRICT (default) x CASCADE (can hit other users' objects); run in each database; does not remove the role's databases/tablespaces; REASSIGN OWNED is the alternative that transfers ownership (PG16 p.1913).

topics.title: dict_xsyn: text search synonym dictionary (PG16 F.14)
topics.summary: Replaces a word with a group of synonyms; options matchorig (true), matchsynonyms (false), keeporig (true), keepsynonyms (true), rules (.rules file in tsearch_data, one word and its synonyms per line, # comments); the extension creates xsyn_template and the xsyn dictionary; test with ts_lexize (PG16 p.2832-2833).

topics.title: Red Book ch. 9: ORMs, CQL (streams), Bloom/CALM and Datalog
topics.summary: Hellerstein's introduction: transactions and declarative languages as abstractions; ORMs (slowness, integrity in the application); CQL = SQL minimally extended for streams and 1st-generation streaming systems with no relevant adoption (p.43); Bloom and CALM: distributed implementation without coordination iff the specification is monotonic (p.43-44); Datalog and Nicira (a billion, informal expression) (p.44) (REDBK p.41-44).

topics.title: JSON functions and operators and the jsonpath type (PG16)
topics.note: 8.14.7 jsonpath starts on p.227 and 9.16 (JSON functions and operators) occupies p.361-380; the package covers only the type, containment and indexing (p.219-225).

topics.title: Reference pages of SQL commands and applications (full map in INDEX.md 3b)
topics.note: The page map of all SQL commands (PG16 p.1562-2071) and client/server applications (p.2072-2285) is in INDEX.md section 3b; use it instead of wide ranges. Summarized in the package: CREATE POLICY (p.1776-1779), CREATE TRIGGER (p.1854-1855), REINDEX (p.1995-1997), reindexdb (p.2226-2227), DROP PUBLICATION/SERVER/SUBSCRIPTION/TABLE/TABLESPACE, CREATE TABLESPACE (p.1842-1843), TRUNCATE (p.2054), CLUSTER (p.1686), CHECKPOINT (p.1684), COPY (p.1697, p.1699, p.1700), pg_dumpall (p.2150-2156), pg_basebackup (p.2099), SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE (p.1999, p.2009-2012), pg_waldump (p.2274-2277), CREATE INDEX (p.1758-1760), CREATE SUBSCRIPTION (p.1811-1814), VACUUM (p.2063-2067), DROP OWNED (p.1913). Also summarized: ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY (p.1648-1649), CREATE PUBLICATION (p.1786-1788), ALTER TABLESPACE (p.1658). The rest (for example the remainder of ALTER TABLE, CREATE TABLE, pg_dump) is pointer only: read the map page.

topics.title: Red Book: chapters without a summary in the package (interactive analytics, ch. 8)
topics.note: Of the Red Book (introductions), only ch. 8 (interactive analytics, p.37-40) remains without a summary. Ch. 5 (p.23-27), 10 (p.3-4), 11 (p.5-9) and 12 (p.10-13) now have a summary (redbook-cap10-11-12-web-analitica-complexa-e-integracao-de-dados.md); ch. 9 in redbook-cap9-linguagens-orm-cql-bloom-datalog.md.

topics.title: Standby, streaming replication, slots, cascading and replication parameters (PG16)
topics.summary: Standby via standby.signal; streaming is asynchronous by default (typical delay < 1 s); slots retain WAL (max_slot_wal_keep_size -1 = unlimited, can fill pg_wal); wal_keep_size 0; max_wal_senders and max_replication_slots 10; cascading is asynchronous; recovery_min_apply_delay for a delayed standby (PG16 p.818-823, p.672-679).

topics.title: Synchronous replication, FIRST/ANY (quorum) and synchronous_commit (PG16)
topics.summary: synchronous_standby_names (empty by default): FIRST n (priority; the next one replaces) and ANY n (quorum); commits may never complete if a synchronous one goes down; name several candidates or reduce/disable and reload; a standby is only synchronous after the streaming state; waiting commits are marked confirmed on primary recovery (it may not be on the standby); minimum wait = round-trip; bandwidth > WAL rate (PG16 p.824-827).

topics.title: Failover, STONITH, witness and degenerate state (PG16)
topics.summary: A primary failure starts failover; the old primary must be notified (STONITH) to avoid two primaries; a witness server avoids certain improper failovers; PostgreSQL does NOT provide the software that detects the failure; degenerate state until the standby is recreated (pg_rewind speeds it up) (PG16 p.827-828).

topics.title: Hot standby: read-only queries, conflicts and administration (PG16)
topics.summary: Hot standby is read-only (no XID, no DML/DDL/2PC/sequences); conflicts with vacuum cleanup and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks cancel queries after max_standby_*_delay (30 s); hot_standby_feedback avoids it, but bloats the primary; memory parameters must be >= those of the primary; Serializable not available (PG16 p.828-835). Note (p.829): before PG 14 in_hot_standby did not exist; the indicated replacement is SHOW transaction_read_only (always true on hot standby); LISTEN/NOTIFY are allowed in normal read-only but not on the standby (PG16 p.829).

topics.title: pg_rewind, wal_log_hints and wal_compression (PG16)
topics.summary: pg_rewind resynchronizes an old primary by copying only changed blocks; requires wal_log_hints or checksums (neither is the default) and full_page_writes=on; target cleanly shut down (otherwise it runs in single-user mode, unless --no-ensure-shutdown); a failure midway leaves the target probably unrecoverable; needs the target's WAL since the divergence or -c (PG16 p.2256-2259, p.665).

topics.title: Logical replication: publication, subscription, filters, conflicts, restrictions and security (PG16 ch. 31)
topics.summary: Publish/subscribe per table based on the replica identity (PK; FULL only as a last resort); DDL, sequences and large objects are not replicated; row filters and column lists (do not use for security); a conflict stops replication and requires manual resolution (SKIP/origin_advance); an orphan slot can fill the disk; wal_level=logical; max_logical_replication_workers 4; sync workers 2 (PG16 p.905-927). Protocol: in the Update message, K (key) only if a column of the replica identity index changed, O (old tuple) only with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, never both (PG16 p.2428).

topics.title: Per-column statistics: SET STATISTICS, n_distinct, ANALYZE on partitioned tables and inheritance (PG16)
topics.summary: SET STATISTICS 0..10000 or -1 (default 100; 0 disables; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock); the largest target defines the sample (no formula in the sources); positive n_distinct = exact, between -1 and 0 = fraction of rows; n_distinct_inherited applies to inheritance and partitioned tables; autovacuum does not analyze partitioned tables (PG16 p.1644, p.1678-1679, p.554, p.685).

topics.title: CREATE STATISTICS and extended statistics: limit on joins (PG16)
topics.summary: CREATE STATISTICS (ndistinct, dependencies, mcv; univariate by expression) on ONE table, by the table owner; collected by ANALYZE; NOT used by the planner when estimating join selectivity across tables (PG16 p.1808).

topics.title: Planner parameters: enable_*, costs, effective_cache_size, join_collapse_limit, GEQO, JIT (PG16)
topics.summary: enable_* are a temporary workaround (enable_indexscan also covers index-only; enable_indexonlyscan requires enable_indexscan on); random_page_cost 4.0; effective_cache_size 4 GB (estimate only); from/join_collapse_limit 8 (1 fixes the JOIN order); GEQO from 12 items; jit on (100000/500000/500000); plan_cache_mode auto; constraint_exclusion partition (PG16 p.680-686).

topics.title: Parallel query, parallel aggregation and parallel safety (PG16 ch. 15)
topics.summary: Gather/Gather Merge; workers limited by max_parallel_workers_per_gather (2), max_parallel_workers (8) and max_worker_processes (8); 2-stage aggregation (Partial/Finalize) does not suit many groups, DISTINCT/ORDER BY, ordered-set and GROUPING SETS, and requires a combine function and all joins in the parallel part; user functions are PARALLEL UNSAFE by default; work_mem applies per worker (PG16 p.564-568, p.660-661).

topics.title: old_snapshot_threshold and the old_snapshot module (PG16)
topics.summary: old_snapshot_threshold: only at startup, default -1 (off), no unit = minutes, useful values hours to a few days; does not guarantee the error; does not return space at the end of the relation to the OS; catalogs are not affected; the old_snapshot module only exposes pg_old_snapshot_time_mapping (PG16 p.661-662, p.2872).

topics.title: PREPARE TRANSACTION, COMMIT PREPARED, ROLLBACK PREPARED and pg_prepared_xacts (PG16)
topics.summary: COMMIT/ROLLBACK PREPARED: same user or superuser, any session, never inside a transaction block, immediate effect; listed in pg_prepared_xacts; GID < 200 bytes; for external managers (XA); forgotten prepared transactions hold locks, block vacuum and can cause wraparound; max_prepared_transactions=0 by default (PG16 p.1695, p.1989-1990, p.2008, p.2577).

topics.title: Table and row locks, LOCK, SKIP LOCKED/NOWAIT and deadlocks (PG16)
topics.summary: Eight table lock modes (only ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocks a plain SELECT; LOCK without a mode = ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; no UNLOCK); four row modes (FOR UPDATE... KEY SHARE; not limited, but they write to disk); deadlock detected after deadlock_timeout (1 s) and resolved by aborting one transaction; avoid with a consistent lock order; SKIP LOCKED suits queues (PG16 p.531-537, p.1972-1974, p.2030). Caveat (PG16 p.538): SELECT FOR UPDATE does not guarantee that a concurrent transaction will not change or delete the row after the lock owner commits/rolls back; only a real UPDATE of the row guarantees that. In RR obtain the locks before the first query; retry 40001 (always), 40P01 and, with care, 23505/23P01 (PG16 p.538-539). 13.6: TRUNCATE/ALTER TABLE that rewrites are not MVCC-safe, Serializable is not supported on hot standby, catalogs are outside isolation (new objects visible to RR/Serializable, rows not). 13.7: B-tree/GiST/SP-GiST use page locks and have no deadlock; hash uses bucket locks and deadlock is possible (PG16 p.539-540).

topics.title: Advisory locks (session-level and transaction-level) and the LIMIT trap (PG16)
topics.summary: Locks with application-defined meaning; session-level (ignore rollback; need unlock) or transaction-level (released at the end); same memory pool as ordinary locks (tens to hundreds of thousands); LIMIT may be applied after the lock function (danger); not WAL-logged or replicated (PG16 p.536-537, p.833-834).

topics.title: Default values: connections and memory (shared_buffers, work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, max_connections) (PG16)
topics.summary: shared_buffers 128 MB (start at 25% of RAM; more than 40% is unlikely to help); work_mem 4 MB per operation (the total can be many times that); hash_mem_multiplier 2.0; maintenance_work_mem 64 MB (VACUUM uses up to 1 GB); max_connections 100; max_prepared_transactions 0; THP discouraged (PG16 p.646-661).

topics.title: Default values: WAL, checkpoints, fsync, archive_timeout and vacuum cost (PG16)
topics.summary: wal_level replica; max_wal_size 1 GB (soft limit); min_wal_size 80 MB; checkpoint_timeout 5 min (30 s to 1 day); completion_target 0.9; wal_buffers -1 (1/32 of shared_buffers, up to 16 MB); fsync/full_page_writes on (turning off can corrupt); empty archive_command accumulates WAL; recovery_target_action pause (PG16 p.658-668, p.672).

topics.title: Default values: statement_timeout, lock_timeout, idle timeouts and freeze age (PG16)
topics.summary: statement_timeout, lock_timeout, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and idle_session_timeout default 0 (disabled; do not set the first two in postgresql.conf); beware of idle_session_timeout and poolers; vacuum_freeze_min_age 50 million, table_age 150 million, failsafe 1.6 billion; log_min_duration_statement -1; log_checkpoints on (PG16 p.690-697, p.702-709, p.715). vacuum_failsafe_age (1.6 billion): effective value at least 105% of autovacuum_freeze_max_age (PG16 p.709); multixact: table_age limited to 95% and min_age to half of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age.

topics.title: Monitoring: pg_stat_activity, pg_stat_database, pg_stat_bgwriter, pg_stat_wal, pg_stat_io and progress (PG16 ch. 28)
topics.summary: pg_stat_activity (state, wait_event, xact_start, backend_xmin; query truncated at 1024 bytes); cumulative counters reset after an unclean shutdown and lag by up to 1 s; pg_stat_replication (lag and sync_state); pg_stat_all_tables (n_dead_tup, n_tup_hot_upd); pg_stat_wal; pg_stat_io; progress views (PG16 p.837-884).

topics.title: Contrib extensions: pg_stat_statements, auto_explain, pg_prewarm, pgstattuple, amcheck, pg_trgm (PG16 appendix F)
topics.summary: pg_stat_statements requires shared_preload_libraries and a restart (max 5000; track_planning off); auto_explain does nothing until log_min_duration is set (-1 by default) and log_analyze has a high cost; pg_prewarm with autoprewarm; pgstattuple measures dead tuples; amcheck verifies B-tree and heap; pg_trgm: similarity and GIN/GiST indexes for LIKE (PG16 appendix F).

topics.title: Data types: ranges and limits of integers, numeric, serial, text, date/time, uuid and money (PG16 ch. 8)
topics.summary: integer +-2.1 billion; numeric up to 131072 digits before the decimal point (declared precision <= 1000); varchar(n) n <= 10485760, maximum value ~1 GB, no performance difference between char/varchar/text; timestamp 4713 BC to 294276 AD, resolution 1 us; serial can have gaps; float is not suitable for money (PG16 p.184-205).

topics.title: Constraints: CHECK, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY (ON DELETE), EXCLUDE and generated columns (PG16 ch. 5.4)
topics.summary: CHECK passes with NULL and cannot reference other rows; NOT NULL is more efficient than CHECK; UNIQUE creates a B-tree and allows several NULLs (NULLS NOT DISTINCT changes this); FK: NO ACTION (deferrable) x RESTRICT x CASCADE; FK does not index the referencing column; EXCLUDE uses an index; generated columns are not replicated (PG16 p.99-110).

topics.title: Other contrib extensions without a summary (pg_visibility, pg_walinspect, postgres_fdw, dblink, pgcrypto, hstore etc.)
topics.note: The manual describes these modules in appendix F (for example pg_walinspect p.2929, postgres_fdw p.2933); the package only mentions them in monitoramento-views-pg-stat-e-extensoes-contrib.md. pageinspect (p.2873-2881) now has a summary (topic pg-pageinspect).

topics.title: Arrays and composite types (PG16 ch. 8.15-8.16)
topics.note: The manual covers arrays (p.229) and composite types (p.238-244) with no summary in the package. Ranges (p.244-248) GOT a summary in round 9 (topic pg-range-types). Only GREATEST/LEAST, the array operators on p.385 and the intarray module (p.2854; topic pg-greatest-arrays-intarray) have a summary.

topics.title: Full text search (tsvector/tsquery) (PG16 ch. 12)
topics.note: The manual devotes ch. 12 (p.483-523) to full text search; the package only points to the GIN/GiST indexes for tsvector (postgresql-16-tipos-de-indices-e-estrategias.md). The tsquery operators and FOLLOWED BY (p.485-486; topic pg-fulltext-followed-by) have a summary. Ranking (ts_rank, ts_rank_cd and normalization, p.493-494; topic pg-fulltext-ranking) has a summary. Pages p.519-520 (12.9, GIN x GiST, ts_lexize) have a summary in the package (topic pg-fulltext-gin-gist). The dict_xsyn dictionary (p.2832-2833; topic pg-dict-xsyn) also has a summary.

topics.title: Client authentication, pg_hba.conf, roles and databases (PG16 ch. 21-23)
topics.note: The manual covers authentication (ch. 21, p.727), roles (ch. 22, p.750) and database management (ch. 23, p.758) with no summary in the package; the package mentions pg_hba only in the replication context. Only cert/clientcert/RADIUS (p.732, p.746-747; topic pg-auth-cert-radius) have a summary. DROP OWNED/REASSIGN OWNED (p.1913; topic pg-drop-owned) also have a summary.

topics.title: Localization, collations and encoding (PG16 ch. 24)
topics.note: The manual covers locale, collation and encoding in ch. 24 (p.764-787) with no summary in the package. Only the pg_collation catalog (p.2309; topic pg-collation-catalog) has a summary.

topics.title: pg_stat_database_conflicts: confl_* columns (recovery conflicts on the standby)
topics.summary: One row per database, has data only on a standby; columns datid, datname and six counters of canceled queries (tablespace, lock, snapshot, bufferpin, deadlock, active_logicalslot); confl_vacuum_cleanup and confl_hot_standby_feedback do not exist (PG16 p.867-868).

topics.title: pageinspect: get_raw_page, page_header, heap, B-tree, BRIN, GIN, GiST
topics.summary: Superuser only; get_raw_page(rel, fork, blkno) returns bytea; heap_page_items shows all tuples (visible or not); bt_* and brin_* inspect indexes; the manual's BRIN example has the inconsistency page 5 x TIDs on page 6 (PG16 p.2873-2879).

topics.title: Configuration file: types, units, postgresql.auto.conf, include, include_if_exists, include_dir, PGOPTIONS
topics.summary: The last value of the parameter wins; include_dir reads only *.conf, ignores names with a dot, in C locale order (numbers before letters, uppercase before lowercase); postgresql.auto.conf (ALTER SYSTEM) takes precedence over postgresql.conf; SIGHUP/pg_reload_conf; -c and PGOPTIONS (PG16 p.641-645).

topics.title: Aggregate functions: Tables 9.59-9.63, count(*), NULL on zero rows, ORDER BY, every, Partial Mode
topics.summary: Zero rows: everything returns NULL except count (sum does not return zero; array_agg does not return an empty array); sum(int)=bigint, sum(bigint)=numeric; undefined order without ORDER BY inside the aggregate; every exists, any/some do not (ambiguity); count(*) scans the whole table or index; Partial Mode Yes in string_agg, No in xmlagg and json_agg (PG16 p.395-402).

topics.title: REINDEX: DATABASE x SYSTEM, CONCURRENTLY, TABLESPACE, partitioned tables, INVALID _ccnew/_ccold
topics.summary: DATABASE does not reindex catalogs and SYSTEM only catalogs (neither in a transaction block); by default it blocks writes and not reads; CONCURRENTLY does two scans and does not run in a transaction; failure leaves an INVALID index (_ccnew: drop; _ccold: drop); TABLESPACE skips catalogs with a WARNING and rebuilds without moving TOAST indexes; partitioned tables per partition in its own transaction (PG16 p.1995-1997). Exclusion constraints are not reindexed CONCURRENTLY (error if named, skipped if table/database); REINDEX SYSTEM without CONCURRENTLY; progress in pg_stat_progress_create_index (PG16 p.1998).

topics.title: reindexdb: REINDEX wrapper, -s/-i/-S/-t/-a, -j incompatible with --index and --system
topics.summary: Just a REINDEX wrapper; -j njobs opens njobs connections (max_connections) and does not combine with --index or --system; --concurrently and --tablespace pass the options on (PG16 p.2226-2227).

topics.title: DROP PUBLICATION, DROP SERVER, DROP SUBSCRIPTION, DROP TABLE, DROP TABLESPACE
topics.summary: DROP PUBLICATION: CASCADE/RESTRICT have no effect (there are no dependencies); DROP SERVER: owner, CASCADE removes user mappings, RESTRICT default, per SQL/MED; DROP SUBSCRIPTION: remote slot, does not run in a transaction if there is a slot; DROP TABLESPACE requires it to be empty and does not run in a transaction (PG16 p.1918-1930).

topics.title: CREATE TABLESPACE: pg_, absolute and empty directory, 4 parameters, outside a transaction
topics.summary: Superuser only; name without the pg_ prefix; LOCATION absolute, existing, empty and owned by the postgres user; WITH accepts seq_page_cost, random_page_cost, effective_io_concurrency, maintenance_io_concurrency; does not run in a transaction block (PG16 p.1842-1843).

topics.title: TRUNCATE, CLUSTER and CHECKPOINT (reference commands)
topics.summary: TRUNCATE: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, does not fire ON DELETE, is not MVCC-safe, transactional; CLUSTER reorders once, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, needs extra space; CHECKPOINT forces a checkpoint (superuser or pg_checkpoint) (PG16 p.1684-2055).

topics.title: Red Book ch. 11: complex analytics (Stonebraker x Hellerstein), arrays, SAS, coupling
topics.summary: Stonebraker: complex analytics is array-oriented and data scientists' platforms are file-based; Table 1 (array x table, loose x tight coupling); seven considerations; Hellerstein (p.8): BI will not be replaced, the incumbent is SAS and whoever uses SAS/R is not a database user; three threats to SAS (REDBK p.5-8).

topics.title: Red Book ch. 12: data integration (ETL, MDM, curation)
topics.summary: ETL scales to a dozen sources for three reasons (global schema up front, manual work, difficulty); MDM is 'overblown'; five steps (ingest, transform, clean, integrate schemas, consolidate); Data Tamer and Data Wrangler; Hellerstein's comment (REDBK p.10-12).

topics.title: Red Book ch. 10: Web data (search engines, PageRank, WebTables)
topics.summary: Search engines: crawlers and read-only indexes; PageRank; Informix 10x slower than Inktomi; WebTables (154 million relations) (REDBK p.3-4).

topics.title: Red Book ch. 5: dataflow engines (MapReduce, Dryad, Spark)
topics.summary: MapReduce as a low-level library; post-MapReduce systems gain SQL and optimizers; three impacts (schema flexibility, interface, architecture); Stonebraker: MapReduce is inadequate, 70% of Spark accesses are SparkSQL (REDBK p.23-26).

topics.title: Recovery parameters: recovery_prefetch, standby.signal x recovery.signal, restore_command (%f %p %r) and WAL/recovery functions (PG16 p.669-670, p.436-437)
topics.summary: standby.signal starts a standby, recovery.signal starts recovery with a target; if both exist, standby prevails; restore_command is mandatory in archive recovery and optional in streaming, with %f (file), %p (destination), %r (last restart point), %% ; recovery_prefetch off/on/try (default try, requires posix_fadvise) and wal_decode_buffer_size (512 kB, startup only); pg_split_walfile_name extracts segment and timeline and the manual's example yields C001/AB000100; pg_last_wal_receive_lsn is NULL without streaming, pg_last_wal_replay_lsn and pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp are NULL on a normal start (PG16 p.669-670, p.436-437).

topics.title: Read-only parameters fixed at compile time: max_index_keys, max_function_args, max_identifier_length, segment_size, integer_datetimes, in_hot_standby (PG16 p.719)
topics.summary: Determined at compile time: max_index_keys 32, max_function_args 100, max_identifier_length 63 bytes (NAMEDATALEN 64 minus 1), segment_size = blocks per file (1 GB by default); integer_datetimes always on since PG 10; in_hot_standby shows whether it is on hot standby; max_partition_keys is not on the page (PG16 p.719).

topics.title: The pg_locks view: locktype (12 values), columns and NULLs (PG16 p.2357-2359)
topics.summary: One row per lockable object, mode and process; locktype: relation, extend, frozenid, page, tuple, transactionid, virtualxid, spectoken, object, userlock, advisory, applytransaction; page/tuple/relation/database/transactionid are NULL when the target is of another type; granted=false indicates waiting; row locks are on disk and normally do not appear; pid NULL for a prepared transaction (PG16 p.2357-2359).

topics.title: pg_verifybackup: stages and options -m, -i, -s, -n, -w (PG16 p.2178-2180)
topics.summary: Verifies a plain backup against backup_manifest in four stages (manifest, files, checksums, WAL via pg_waldump); -m uses another manifest, -i/--ignore suppresses complaints about a file or directory, -s/--skip-checksums does not compute checksums but still checks file presence and size; postgresql.auto.conf, standby.signal, recovery.signal, backup_manifest and pg_wal do not cause complaints; does not replace a test restore (PG16 p.2178-2180).

topics.title: pg_receivewal: default flush, --synchronous, synchronous standby with remote_apply, starting point (PG16)
topics.summary: pg_receivewal flushes only when closing the file (use --synchronous for real time); it does not apply WAL, so as a synchronous standby with remote_apply it blocks commits; the manual's three ways out (p.2159): a suitable synchronous_standby_names, an application_name that does not match, or synchronous_commit other than remote_apply; starting point in 3 steps (last complete segment, slot restart_lsn in PG 15+, IDENTIFY_SYSTEM); infinite reconnection, -n exits right away (PG16 p.2159-2161).

topics.title: Event triggers: events, what does not fire, pg_event_trigger_* functions, aborted transaction, order (PG16 ch. 40)
topics.summary: Four events (ddl_command_start, ddl_command_end, table_rewrite, sql_drop; there is no ddl_command_abort); they do not fire for databases, roles and tablespaces or for event triggers; table_rewrite does not fire for CLUSTER/VACUUM; an aborted transaction does not execute them; failure at start prevents the command; failure at end undoes the DDL; alphabetical order; cannot be written in plain SQL (PG16 p.1312-1313).

topics.title: REVOKE: CASCADE, grant option, non-owner, superuser, several role paths and SET ROLE (PG16)
topics.summary: Dependent privileges only drop with CASCADE (otherwise the REVOKE fails); a non-owner revokes only what they granted; a superuser acts as the owner and may need CASCADE; with several role paths the role used is unspecified and SET ROLE is recommended; default RESTRICT (PG16 p.2004-2005).

topics.title: Full text search: ts_rank, ts_rank_cd, weights and normalization mask 0/1/2/4/8/16/32 (PG16)
topics.summary: Normalization is a bit mask (0 default ignores length; 1, 2, 4 only in ts_rank_cd, 8, 16, 32); applied in the listed order; 32 = rank/(rank+1) and is only cosmetic; no global information; default weights {0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 1.0} in the order D, C, B, A (PG16 p.493-494).

topics.title: SQL key words (Appendix C): actual PostgreSQL 16 classifications (reserved, non-reserved, requires AS, can/cannot be function or type)
topics.summary: Table C.1: columns PostgreSQL, SQL:2023, SQL:2016 and SQL-92; ~100 reserved (lists by class in the summary), ~370 non-reserved, blank cell = identifier; 'requires AS'; reserved 'can be function or type' (INNER, JOIN, LEFT...); HAVING, INITIALLY, INNER reserved; INCLUDE, INDEX, INOUT non-reserved (PG16 p.2624, p.2633, p.2645).

topics.title: libpq: single-row mode (PQsetSingleRowMode) and rows already delivered when the query fails (PG16)
topics.summary: In single-row mode rows arrive one by one (PGRES_SINGLE_TUPLE); if the query fails later, the rows were already delivered (libpq normally discards them) and the application must discard or undo whatever it did with them (PG16 p.995-996).

topics.title: Transaction management in PL/pgSQL: COMMIT/ROLLBACK in procedures (CALL/DO) (PG16 43.8)
topics.summary: COMMIT/ROLLBACK only in top-level or nested CALL/DO with no command in between (CALL->SELECT func->CALL does not work); a new transaction starts automatically (there is no START TRANSACTION in PL/pgSQL); COMMIT AND CHAIN preserves characteristics; a loop cursor becomes holdable at the first COMMIT; forbidden in a loop over a non-read-only command (UPDATE ... RETURNING) and in a block with an exception handler (PG16 p.1389-1390).

topics.title: Appendix B: date/time input, two-digit year and daylight saving time (DST)
topics.summary: Heuristic parser in 5 steps (time/date/time zone token, time zone abbreviation, number by digits, BC, 2-digit year: <70 adds 2000, otherwise 1900); field out of range = error; a nonexistent/ambiguous timestamp at a DST transition is not rejected: invalid on a forward jump gets the offset from before, ambiguous on the way back gets the offset from after (preference for standard time); 3 examples from America/New_York (PG16 p.2616-2617). B.4-B.5 (p.2620-2622): POSIX time zone 'STD offset [DST [dstoffset] [,rule]]' with a positive sign = west of Greenwich (the inverse of ISO-8601); rule dstdate[/time],stddate[/time] in n (0-364), Jn (1-365 without Feb 29) or Mm.n.d (n=5 last); default time 02:00:00; default rule M3.2.0,M11.1.0 = US 2020, wrong before 2007; EST5EDT/CST6CDT/MST7MDT/PST8PDT are named IANA zones (historical US transitions correct); no validation: TIMEZONE FOOBAR0 works (PG16 p.2620-2622).

topics.title: Range types and multirange: inclusive/exclusive bounds, infinity, quoting, constructors, discrete
topics.summary: Range = a span of an orderable subtype; [ and ] inclusive, ( and ) exclusive; omitted bound = unbounded and [,] becomes (,), distinct from the subtype's infinity ([today,infinity) excludes infinity); quotes for parentheses/brackets/commas/quotes/backslashes (space is not listed), empty string = ""; 2-arg constructor = [); discrete (int, date) canonicalize to [); multirange (PG16 p.244-248).

topics.title: Full text search: tsquery operators, FOLLOWED BY (<->, <N>, <0>), precedence and semantics of !x <-> y
topics.summary: <-> requires adjacent lexemes in order; <N> = position difference (<2> allows one lexeme in between; phraseto_tsquery uses it for stop words); <0> = same word; precedence | < & < <-> < !; inside FOLLOWED BY position matters: !x <-> y matches y that does not come right after x, and (x & y) <-> z requires x and y at the same position (PG16 p.485-486).

topics.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE: measurement artifacts (merge join, BitmapAnd/Or, LIMIT, Subplans Removed) and reltuples/relpages
topics.summary: Merge join stops reading when the other input ends and rereads the inner child for duplicate keys of the outer (inflated actual rows); BitmapAnd/BitmapOr always show 0 actual rows (only those; Bitmap Index Scan shows the count); LIMIT makes actual < estimated without error; Subplans Removed only in Append/MergeAppend of partitioned tables; reltuples/relpages are updated by VACUUM/ANALYZE/CREATE INDEX (incrementally if it does not scan everything) and the planner scales to the physical size (PG16 p.552-553).

topics.title: Dependency tracking: the group rule in DROP and functions with string body x BEGIN ATOMIC
topics.summary: DROP with several objects: CASCADE only if the dependency comes from outside the group (DROP TABLE tab1, tab2 with an FK from tab2 to tab1 does not require it); a function with a string body tracks argument/result types but not the table in the body (dropping the table does not drop the function); BEGIN ATOMIC keeps the body's dependencies and DROP enforces them (PG16 p.147).

topics.title: pg_buffercache: view, pg_buffercache_summary() and pg_buffercache_usage_counts(); buffer manager locks
topics.summary: View with one row per buffer; NONE of the three forms takes buffer manager locks (the view has less impact but the result is not consistent across buffers; summary() and usage_counts() are significantly cheaper and may have small inaccuracies); join with pg_class restricting reldatabase to the current database or 0; access for superuser/pg_monitor (PG16 p.2885-2887).

topics.title: SELECT FOR UPDATE is not enough: the 13.4.2 caveat and the 13.5 retry (PG16 p.538-539)
topics.summary: SELECT FOR UPDATE blocks UPDATE/DELETE and other locks only while the lock lasts; when the owner commits/rolls back, the blocked one proceeds with the conflicting operation, unless a real UPDATE of the row was made (PG16 p.538). Two SELECT sum() in RC are not reliable; a single RR gives a snapshot from before the start; SHARE+ guarantees there are no uncommitted changes; in RR obtain the lock before the first query. Retry 40001 always; 40P01 and 23505/23P01 with care; retry the whole transaction; there is no automatic retry (PG16 p.538-539).

topics.title: pg_waldump: timeline (-t), .partial files, -s/-e, filters (PG16 p.2274-2277)
topics.summary: Shows WAL in readable form; only the user who installed the server; -t/--timeline (default = startseg or 1; only the requested timeline is displayed, the others are ignored); does NOT read .partial files: the suffix must be removed from the name (on a copy, inference); -s/-e LSN, -n, -f, -r rmgr, -R, -B, -F, -x, -w, -z; can give wrong results with the server running (PG16 p.2274-2277).

topics.title: pg_dumpall: globals, superuser, --no-role-passwords, --no-sync, --on-conflict-do-nothing (PG16 p.2150-2156)
topics.summary: Dump of the whole cluster by calling pg_dump per database and including roles, tablespaces and parameter grants; needs a superuser for dump and restore; --no-role-passwords leaves the password null and reads pg_roles instead of pg_authid; --no-sync does not wait for fsync (risk of a corrupted dump after a crash; test only); --on-conflict-do-nothing only with --inserts/--column-inserts; -g/-r/-t; --clean recreates postgres and template1; restore with psql -X (PG16 p.2150-2156).

topics.title: log_startup_progress_interval, application_name and Table 20.2 (PG16 p.692-693)
topics.summary: log_startup_progress_interval: default 10 s, 0 turns it off, no unit = ms, per operation, only postgresql.conf/command line; application_name < NAMEDATALEN (64), printable ASCII; Table 20.2 translates severities to syslog/eventlog (WARNING becomes NOTICE in syslog) (PG16 p.692-693).

topics.title: round, trunc, scale, trim_scale, width_bucket and random (PG16 p.266-267)
topics.summary: round: numeric ties away from zero, double depends on the platform; trunc toward zero; scale counts decimal places, trim_scale removes zeros; width_bucket returns 0 below low and count+1 from high, the threshold array must be sorted; random() in [0,1), setseed in [-1,1], not suitable for cryptography (PG16 p.266-267).

topics.title: Appendix D.2: T176 NEXT VALUE FOR, T180/T181 temporal, T218 trigger order (PG16 p.2665)
topics.summary: D.2 lists SQL:2023 features not implemented: T176 sequences supported except NEXT VALUE FOR; T180 (system versioning) and T181 (application periods) without comment; T175 generated columns mostly supported; T200 trigger DDL similar but not fully compatible; T218 (several triggers in creation order) intentionally omitted; T301 and T321 partial (PG16 p.2665).

topics.title: Transaction ID and snapshot functions, deprecated txid_* and commit timestamp (PG16 p.428-430)
topics.summary: txid_* are the old versions (bigint, txid_snapshot; before PG 13), deprecated but still supported and may go away; replacements pg_current_xact_id, pg_current_snapshot, pg_snapshot_*, pg_visible_in_snapshot, pg_xact_status (PG16 p.430). pg_xact_commit_timestamp, _origin and pg_last_committed_xact only return data with track_commit_timestamp on (default off) and only for transactions committed afterwards; vacuum removes the information; there is no track_commit_timestamp_retention or _batch() (PG16 p.430).

topics.title: ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY: DEFAULT, USING INDEX, FULL, NOTHING (PG16 p.1648-1649)
topics.summary: DEFAULT records the old values of the primary key columns (default on non-system tables); USING INDEX requires a unique, non-partial, non-deferrable index with only NOT NULL columns, and if the index is dropped it becomes NOTHING; FULL records all columns; NOTHING is the default for system tables. Only has an effect with logical replication. The old value is only logged if it differs from the new one, unless it is in TOAST (always logged) (PG16 p.1648-1649).

topics.title: CREATE PUBLICATION: what is included, column list x schema, partitions, publish and publish_via_partition_root (PG16 p.1786-1788)
topics.summary: Only persistent base tables and partitioned tables; temporary, unlogged, foreign tables, matviews and views are not included. A column list together with FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA is not supported (in either direction). Existing and future partitions are included implicitly, even from another schema. publish only affects DML, not the initial copy; publish_via_partition_root default false; no recommendation to always use true (PG16 p.1786-1788).

topics.title: libpq: connect_timeout, keepalives, PQconnectPoll (PG16 p.950, p.958-959)
topics.summary: connect_timeout in seconds: zero, negative or absent = wait indefinitely; minimum 2 s (1 becomes 2); applies per host/IP, so N hosts = up to N x timeout; ignored with PQconnectPoll (p.950). keepalives default 1, ignored on a Unix socket; keepalives_idle/interval/count: 0 = system default (PG16 p.958-959). Server-side tcp_keepalives_*: p.648.

topics.title: Protocol: CopyData, CopyDone, CopyFail, CopyInResponse messages and copy-in/out/both modes (PG16 p.2389-2390, p.2412-2413)
topics.summary: CopyData d, CopyDone c, CopyFail f (client only, carries an error string), CopyInResponse G, CopyOutResponse H, CopyBothResponse W; overall format 0/1, number of columns and per-column codes; if the overall format is textual all codes are 0; the backend sends one row per CopyData; the client does not abort copy-out (PG16 p.2389-2390, p.2412-2413).

topics.title: Catalog views pg_matviews and pg_policies (PG16 p.2360)
topics.summary: pg_matviews: null tablespace = database default; hasindexes (has or recently had indexes); ispopulated (currently populated). pg_policies: permissive (permissive or restrictive), qual (security barrier), with_check (WITH CHECK of commands that add rows) (PG16 p.2360).

topics.title: Tablespaces: pg_tblspc, pg_global/pg_default, database catalogs and DROP (PG16 p.762-763, p.1658, p.1930)
topics.summary: Database catalogs live in the database's tablespace (without TABLESPACE the template's is used); pg_global holds shared catalogs, pg_default is the default of template1/template0; DROP requires the tablespace to be empty in all databases; links in pg_tblspc can be adjusted by hand (not recommended, never with the server running); in 9.1 and earlier also update pg_tablespace (PG16 p.762-763, p.1930).

topics.title: B-tree deduplication: posting lists, deduplicate_items, types that do not deduplicate, cost and decision time (PG16 p.2513-2514)
topics.summary: Merges leaf duplicates into a posting list (value once + ordered TIDs); on by default; CREATE INDEX/REINDEX merge on sorted input; a write load without duplicates pays a small fixed penalty, reads never; deduplicate_items=off per index; in UNIQUE it absorbs version churn; safety decided at CREATE INDEX/REINDEX; do not deduplicate: nondeterministic collation, numeric, jsonb, float4/float8, containers (arrays, composites, ranges), INCLUDE (PG16 p.2513-2514).

topics.title: Rule system (ch. 41): view = empty table + _RETURN rule, ON SELECT, CREATE RULE, order and warnings (PG16 p.1322, p.1332-1333)
topics.summary: View = empty table without storage with an ON SELECT DO INSTEAD rule (_RETURN); a table cannot have an ON SELECT rule; ON SELECT has a single unconditional INSTEAD SELECT action and is applied last, even in INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; update rules can have zero, one or several actions and qualification with NEW/OLD; volatile functions may run more times and WITH is not supported: prefer triggers; ON INSERT runs the original before, ON UPDATE/DELETE after (PG16 p.1322, p.1332-1333).

topics.title: Window function calls (4.2.8): default frame, ROWS/RANGE/GROUPS, FILTER, restrictions and where they appear (PG16 p.86-88)
topics.summary: Default frame RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING (with ORDER BY up to the last peer; without ORDER BY the whole partition); ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 8 PRECEDING is allowed, RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND offset PRECEDING is not; FILTER only on window functions that are aggregates; ordered-set/hypothetical-set aggregates do not work as windows; window-specific functions accept neither DISTINCT nor ORDER BY; calls only in SELECT and ORDER BY (PG16 p.86-88).

topics.title: pg_dump and pg_restore: --create, formats, -j, continuing after errors and superuser warning (PG16 p.2135-2136, p.2169-2170)
topics.summary: pg_dump dumps one database (roles and tablespaces belong to pg_dumpall); parallel dump only in directory format; custom and directory allow selective and parallel restore; pg_restore --create uses -d only for DROP/CREATE DATABASE and restores the data into the archive's database, plus comment, ALTER DATABASE SET and ACL (unless --no-acl); the default is to continue after an error and count at the end (-e exits); the format is detected automatically; -j only custom/directory, regular file; restoring a dump runs arbitrary code from the source superusers (PG16 p.2135-2136, p.2169-2170).

topics.title: interval: input, months/days/microseconds fields, fractions, sign and IntervalStyle (PG16 p.202-204)
topics.summary: Verbose, short (1 12:59:10; 200-10) and ISO 8601 input; INTERVAL '1' = 1 second, INTERVAL '1' YEAR = 1 year; fields to the right of the least significant are discarded (HOUR TO MINUTE loses seconds, not the day); a leading sign applies only to the days in the default style and to all in sql_standard; stored as months, days and microseconds; fractions of units larger than a month become months, of weeks/days become days and microseconds (30 days/month, 24 h/day); four output styles, default postgres (PG16 p.202-204).

topics.title: float4/float8: shortest precise output, extra_float_digits, range and special values (PG16 p.188-189)
topics.summary: Default output = the shortest precise decimal representation (up to 17 digits in float8 and 9 in float4); extra_float_digits = 0 restores the old rounding (6 and 15 digits), negative reduces, greater than 0 selects the shortest precise format, and 3 is still recommended for compatibility; real ~1E-37..1E+37 (>= 6 digits), double ~1E-307..1E+308 (>= 15); Infinity, -Infinity and NaN with quotes; NaN equals NaN and is greater than everything; money uses numeric; float equality can fail (PG16 p.188-189).

topics.title: Appendix D and D.1: degree of conformance, parts covered, 170 of 177 Core, subfeatures and E021-04 (PG16 p.2649-2650)
topics.summary: Appendix D is not a complete conformance statement; Core = mandatory features, the rest is optional; the core covers parts 1, 2, 9, 11 and 14 (3 via ODBC and 13 via PL/Java unverified; 4, 10, 15 and 16 nonexistent); of 177 mandatory Core features PostgreSQL meets at least 170 and no DBMS claims full conformance to SQL:2023 Core; approximate lists; a code with a hyphen = subfeature (without it, the main feature is unsupported); E021-04 trims trailing spaces of CHARACTER before counting (PG16 p.2649-2650).

topics.title: pg_isready: exit codes 0/1/2/3, timeout and note on invalid credentials (PG16 p.2157-2158)
topics.summary: 0 = accepting connections; 1 = rejecting connections (e.g.: during startup); 2 = no response; 3 = no attempt (invalid parameters); -t default 3 s, 0 disables; does not require a correct user, password or database, but incorrect values produce a connection failure record in the server log (PG16 p.2157-2158).

topics.title: UPDATE: FROM x sub-SELECT, not repeating the target table, multiple matching rows, SAVEPOINT example and compatibility (PG16 p.2058-2062)
topics.summary: With FROM the target is joined to the from_item tables; the join must yield at most one row per target row, otherwise only one is used, unpredictably; a sub-SELECT is safer (error if several rows); do not repeat the target table in FROM, except for a self-join with an alias; FROM and RETURNING are PostgreSQL extensions and the manual warns that this is not how PostgreSQL interprets FROM when another DBMS requires repeating the target; manual example with SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO sp1 to insert or update without failing the transaction (PG16 p.2058-2062).

topics.title: Multixacts: member storage (10 GB and 20 GB), warnings at 40 million, refusal below 3 million and recovery (PG16)
topics.summary: A multixact ID replaces several transactions in xmax; member list in pg_multixact with a 32-bit counter; aggressive vacuum if age > autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age (400 million) or if members exceed ~10 GB (even with autovacuum off); members reach ~20 GB before wraparound; warnings at 40 million; refusal of new MXIDs below 3 million; recovery as with XID, but slots do not hold multixacts and only transactions with a row lock that requires an MXID block (PG16 p.795-796).

topics.title: Actual vacuum cost delay: delay x balance / limit, cap of 4 x delay, delay < 1 ms (PG16)
topics.summary: Operations holding critical locks do not sleep and the cost accumulates beyond the limit; effective delay = vacuum_cost_delay * balance / vacuum_cost_limit, at most vacuum_cost_delay * 4; typical values below 1 ms (PG16 p.658).

topics.title: session_replication_role: origin, replica, local; who changes it; plan discard; FKs (PG16)
topics.summary: Values origin (default), replica and local; origin and local are treated the same internally; only superusers and those with the SET privilege change it; changing it discards cached plans; replica disables triggers, rules and FKs (PG16 p.707).

topics.title: pg_rewrite catalog, pg_rules view and relhasrules (PG16)
topics.summary: pg_rewrite: rulename, ev_class, ev_type (1 SELECT, 2 UPDATE, 3 INSERT, 4 DELETE), ev_enabled (O, D, R, A), is_instead, ev_qual, ev_action; no ev_priority; relhasrules (has or once had rules); pg_rules excludes ON SELECT rules of views (PG16 p.2308, p.2333, p.2365, p.2374).

topics.title: Release notes for 16 (E.16): logical replication (PG16)
topics.summary: Decoding on standbys, parallel apply, binary copy, REPLICA IDENTITY FULL with btree, ORIGIN option, run_as_owner and the table owner, wal_retrieve_retry_interval per subscription (PG16 p.2753-2754).

topics.title: Release notes for 16 (E.16): utility commands and types (PG16)
topics.summary: EXPLAIN GENERIC_PLAN, COPY FROM with DEFAULT, batch_size, STORAGE in CREATE TABLE, VACUUM TOAST only, SKIP_DATABASE_STATS, REINDEX without argument, CREATE STATISTICS with automatic name, integer literals 0x/0o/0b (PG16 p.2754).

topics.title: postgres -C: runtime parameter, stopped server and use by programs (PG16)
topics.summary: -C prints the parameter value and exits, ignores parameters given when starting the cluster, requires the server to be shut down for computed parameters (shared_memory_size, shared_memory_size_in_huge_pages, wal_segment_size); applications use SHOW or pg_settings (PG16 p.2279).

topics.title: Restoring a text dump: ON_ERROR_STOP, exit status 3, -1 and pg_dump | psql pipe (PG16)
topics.summary: ON_ERROR_STOP makes psql exit with status 3 on an SQL error; -1 restores in a single transaction; pipe pg_dump -h host1 dbname | psql -X -h host2 dbname (PG16 p.801).

topics.title: Protocol: canceling an in-progress request (CancelRequest, BackendKeyData) (PG16 p.2382, p.2391, p.2410)
topics.summary: Cancellation does not go over the query's connection (the backend does not keep checking input): the client opens a NEW connection and sends CancelRequest in place of the StartupMessage; no direct response; only valid with the PID and secret key from BackendKeyData; Int32(16), code 80877102 (1234 in the high 16 bits, 5678 in the low ones), PID, key; it may have no effect and the client does not know whether it worked; any process can issue it (PG16 p.2382, p.2391, p.2410).

topics.title: SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT and RELEASE SAVEPOINT: repeated name and compatibility (PG16 p.1999, p.2009-2012)
topics.summary: Repeated name: the old savepoint becomes inaccessible until the new one is released; ROLLBACK TO uses the most recent and KEEPS the savepoint (destroys only those created later), RELEASE releases the named one and later ones and the old one becomes accessible again; the SQL standard would destroy the old one, PostgreSQL keeps it; cursors do not have their FETCH undone (PG16 p.1999, p.2009-2012).

topics.title: pg_basebackup: whole cluster, walsenders, backup from a standby (PG16 p.2099)
topics.summary: Backup is always of the whole cluster, over a replication connection (REPLICATION + pg_hba); max_wal_senders: one walsender for the backup plus one for WAL streaming (if used), so 1 with -X none; from a standby it requires hot_standby and full_page_writes on the primary, does not create the backup history file, does not force a WAL switch on the standby (use pg_switch_wal on the primary with -X none) and fails if the standby is promoted; --switch-wal-on-standby and backup_standby_timeout do not exist (PG16 p.2099).

topics.title: --restrict-key and --rows-per-insert in pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore (PG16 p.2144, p.2153-2154, p.2173)
topics.summary: --restrict-key=key fixes the key of psql's \restrict (alphanumeric only; without it, a random key); intended for tests and repeatable output (e.g.: comparing dumps), not recommended for general use because a malicious server that knows the key can inject code; pg_dump only in plain text, pg_restore only with --file. --rows-per-insert=n generates INSERTs of up to n rows (n > 0); an error loses only the rows of that INSERT (PG16 p.2144, p.2153-2154, p.2173).

topics.title: Identifiers (NAMEDATALEN, 63 bytes) and PostgreSQL limits Table K.1 (PG16 p.72, p.3001)
topics.summary: Identifier: at most NAMEDATALEN-1 = 63 bytes, truncated if longer, quotes do not change the limit, recompile to change (pg_config_manual.h); Table K.1: 1,600 columns per table, 1,664 in a result, field 1 GB, relation 32 TB, 32 columns per index, 32 partition keys, 100 function arguments, 65,535 query parameters, 2^32 out-of-line values per table (PG16 p.72, p.3001).

topics.title: Background worker processes: registration, bgw_*, restart, WaitLatch, handle and LISTEN (PG16 p.1529-1531)
topics.summary: User processes started and monitored by the postmaster, with shared memory and an internal connection to a database; RegisterBackgroundWorker (postmaster) x RegisterDynamicBackgroundWorker (backend); exit with code 0, BGW_NEVER_RESTART or TerminateBackgroundWorker unregisters, otherwise it restarts; to pause use WaitLatch with WL_POSTMASTER_DEATH; GetBackgroundWorkerPid/BGWH_*, WaitForBackgroundWorkerStartup/Shutdown; do not use LISTEN in a worker (PG16 p.1529-1531).

topics.title: Logical replication: column lists (partition root, identity, TRUNCATE, subscriber < 15) and MERGE/ON CONFLICT in 16.11 (PG16 p.920-921, p.2698)
keywords: on conflict do update replica identity
topics.summary: Column list: with published UPDATE/DELETE it must include the replica identity; partitioned tables use the root's list if publish_via_partition_root=true and each partition's if false; no effect on TRUNCATE; a subscriber older than 15 copies all columns in the initial load; changing the lists of already subscribed publications can cause an error on the subscriber (way out: equalize the lists and recreate the subscription or ALTER SUBSCRIPTION DROP PUBLICATION). In 16.11, MERGE and INSERT ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE require REPLICA IDENTITY when the table publishes updates/deletes (or inserts/updates) (PG16 p.920-921, p.2698).

topics.title: TOAST: per-column COMPRESSION, default_toast_compression and the 1-byte varlena header (PG16 p.2570, p.706, p.1644, p.1819)
topics.summary: Per-column COMPRESSION (CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE ... SET COMPRESSION: pglz or lz4, or default); without a choice, default_toast_compression at INSERT time applies; SET COMPRESSION does not rewrite the table; values < 127 bytes use a 1-byte varlena header, with no alignment (PG16 p.2570, p.706, p.1644, p.1819).

topics.title: pg_stat_io: omitted rows, NULL cells and the track_io_timing note; bgwriter x checkpoint (PG16 p.864, p.659, p.667)
topics.summary: Rows for backend types that never do a given I/O are omitted; operations that never occur appear as NULL (fsyncs of temp relations; reads by the background writer); time columns are non-null only with track_io_timing, and comparison requires it to have been on since the last reset; bgwriter parameters are on p.659 and checkpoint ones on p.667 (PG16 p.864, p.659, p.667).
